exam.title: Linux Foundation Certified System Administrator
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite; practical readiness requires repeated command-line administration on fresh systems. Practice persistent kernel/services/jobs/packages and recovery; libvirt, containers and SELinux; dual-stack networking, SSH, filtering/NAT/routes/bridges/bonds/proxies; LVM/filesystems/swap/automount/NFS/NBD; Git, certificates, services/performance/disk troubleshooting; and local/LDAP identities, profiles, limits and ACLs.

review.notes: All five current distribution-independent domains are mapped to runtime state, persistent configuration, restart/reboot/recreate and revalidation, with three operational scenarios, eight safe labs and 40 original checks. All six guide URLs are cataloged: five reachable and O'Reilly automation-blocked; none missing or broken. No proprietary simulator tasks, course labs or recalled exam tasks are used.

findings.title: Active unit state does not always mean a running process
findings.evidence: A successful oneshot with RemainAfterExit can remain active after its process exits; without it a completed oneshot can become inactive.
findings.recommendation: Correct the guide answer, add an explicitly unexecuted Linux state exercise and require application-specific readiness evidence.
findings.resolution: Correct the guide answer, add an explicitly unexecuted Linux state exercise and require application-specific readiness evidence.

findings.title: Persistent timer catch-up is not a queue of all missed invocations
findings.evidence: Persistent affects OnCalendar timers and an already-active service is not restarted for a timer event.
findings.recommendation: Clarify catch-up and overlap behavior, including why an indefinitely active oneshot can prevent repeated runs.
findings.resolution: Clarify catch-up and overlap behavior, including why an indefinitely active oneshot can prevent repeated runs.

findings.title: Persistent domain configuration does not require automatic startup
findings.evidence: The reference separates definition, transient or one-time running configuration and autostart requirements.
findings.recommendation: Correct the readiness answer and require the requested live/saved/autostart behavior instead of always enabling autostart.
findings.resolution: Correct the readiness answer and require the requested live/saved/autostart behavior instead of always enabling autostart.

findings.title: Certificate checks cover different conditions
findings.evidence: Name, trust, application purpose and reference time are explicit verification parameters; an expiry-window check is not complete validation.
findings.recommendation: Execute independent positive/negative certificate checks and real verified/rejected TLS handshakes without changing system trust or clock.
findings.resolution: Execute independent positive/negative certificate checks and real verified/rejected TLS handshakes without changing system trust or clock.

findings.title: Upstream resize capabilities differ from blanket historical rules
findings.evidence: The current upstream manual describes mounted growth and restricted last-allocation-group shrinking; geometry and installed stack support still matter.
findings.recommendation: Avoid a universal never-shrink claim and require target kernel/xfsprogs/distribution support review; no resize executed.
findings.resolution: Avoid a universal never-shrink claim and require target kernel/xfsprogs/distribution support review; no resize executed.

findings.title: Matching named-user denial does not fall back to other
findings.evidence: The access algorithm evaluates a matching named-user entry and mask before group/other classes; owner is not mask-capped.
findings.recommendation: Add an original effective-bit example and operation-specific access evidence without claiming Windows reproduces native ACL behavior.
findings.resolution: Add an original effective-bit example and operation-specific access evidence without claiming Windows reproduces native ACL behavior.

findings.title: Identity lookup success does not establish secure login
findings.evidence: SSSD documents different TLS behavior for LDAP identity and authentication paths, plus schema-dependent group mapping.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish lookup, authentication, authorization and session setup; require certificate trust for the configured paths and retain local recovery.
findings.resolution: Distinguish lookup, authentication, authorization and session setup; require certificate trust for the configured paths and retain local recovery.

findings.title: SSH syntax validation does not prove the intended account can log in
findings.evidence: Test mode checks configuration/key sanity, while extended test mode with connection parameters displays applicable effective settings.
findings.recommendation: Add test-mode versus actual login distinctions and preserve recovery access during changes.
findings.resolution: Add test-mode versus actual login distinctions and preserve recovery access during changes.

local_validation.execution_boundary: Git for Windows OpenSSL CLI, Windows Python SSL and MSYS Bash; synthetic disposable CA/CSR/certificates/keys, loopback-only port chosen by OS, context-specific trust only, temporary files cleaned. No system/browser trust, DNS, host clock, global OpenSSL configuration, external service, credential, Linux service/storage/network/ACL/SELinux/VM/container changes. No revocation, intermediate-chain, mTLS, HTTP, remote deployment or native Linux lab executed.

limitations: Same-context AI review; independent human review pending.
38 local checks passed with Git for Windows OpenSSL3.5.7, Python3.13.14 linkedOpenSSL3.0.21 and MSYS Bash; exact public examples are hash-matched.
Six real loopback TLS attempts: two validated payload exchanges and four intended hostname/trust rejections; workers and listeners stopped, owned keys/certificates/files cleaned.

No system/browser trust, DNS, host clock, global OpenSSL configuration, real credentials, external endpoints, Linux services/storage/network/ACL/SELinux, VMs or containers changed. All eight complete Linux labs remain proposed.

Native Linux runtime remains blocked from the earlier WSL startup attempt and is deferred for tomorrow; Windows/MSYS is not proof of Linux administration, filesystem, networking or mandatory-access behavior.
No revocation, intermediate CA chain, mutual TLS, HTTP/proxy, production PKI or remote deployment tested. Expiry and other reference-time checks did not change the operating-system clock.
Extent/throughput/capacity, route-selection and ACL calculations are deliberately restricted original models, not actual kernel/storage/permission tests.
Upstream documentation may be newer than an exam/distribution runtime; limited XFS shrinking and systemd syntax need installed-version and support verification.
Public catalog metadata only; OReilly blocked, old runtime/date claims unverified, mixed course dates/outline labels qualified. No paid lessons, simulator questions or provider labs accessed.
